facts.statement: Yixianopterus is a pterosaur genus found in the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Yixianopterus is a pterodactyloid pterosaur genus from the Barremian-Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single holotype specimen, JZMP-V-12, housed at the Benxi Geological Museum.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen, holotype JZMP-V-12, housed at the Benxi Geological Museum.

facts.statement: The specimen was found in Jinggangshan bedding consisting of basaltic and siliciclastic sediments.
facts.quote: The Jinggangshan bedding in which the specimen was found is basaltic with siliciclastic sediments.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in the uppermost layer of the Yixian Formation known as the Jinggangshan bedding.
facts.quote: Holotype JZMP-V-12 was discovered within the Jinggangshan bedding, the uppermost layer of the Yixian Formation.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest of the upper humerus extended 25.38 mm, a feature characterizing the specimen as belonging to Pteranodontoidea.
facts.quote: The deltopectoral crest of the upper humerus, extending a quarter of the length (25.38mm), characterized the specimen as belonging to Pteranodontoidea.

facts.statement: Metatarsal III measures 28.19 mm in length, while the preserved portion of the tibia is 102.63 mm long.
facts.quote: Metatarsal III is 28.19mm long while what was preserved of the tibia is 102.63 mm in length.

facts.statement: The teeth were subequal with the diastema increasing posteriorly, as noted by Lü et al. (2006).
facts.quote: Lü et al. (2006) noted that the teeth of the specimen were subequal with diastema increasing posteriorly.

facts.statement: An outline of the head preserved in the sediment showed a dorsal inclination.
facts.quote: An outline of the head preserved within the sediment showed a dorsal inclination.

facts.statement: The skull is elongated and flat, without a crest, with a preserved length of approximately 25 centimeters.
facts.quote: El cráneo es alargado y plano, sin cresta, con una longitud conservada de aproximadamente 25 centímetros.

facts.statement: The skull ends in a blunt tip and has short front teeth that are perpendicular to the jawline.
facts.quote: El cráneo del fósil termina en una punta roma y dientes delanteros cortos que son perpendiculares a la línea de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The wings are relatively long and robustly built, with a relatively short fourth metacarpal bone.
facts.quote: Las alas son relativamente largas y de constitución robusta, con el cuarto hueso metacarpiano relativamente corto.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan is about 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: La envergadura alar estimada es de unos 3,5 metros.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that due to its large wings and elongated head, Yixianopterus was likely a specialized glider that fed on fish.
facts.quote: Dado que tenía grandes alas y una cabeza alargada es probable que Yixianopterus fuera un especializado planeador que se alimentaba de peces.

facts.statement: Lü et al. (2006) assigned Yixianopterus to the family Lonchodectidae based on dental characters and bone ratio comparisons.
facts.quote: Lü et al. (2006) assigned Yixianopterus to the Lophocratian family Lonchodectidae based on dental characters, and ratio comparisons between wing phalanx I and II, metacarpal IV, and ulna.

facts.statement: Martill (2011) considered it potentially related to Unwindia, while Witton (2013) assigned it to the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Martill (2011) considered it potentially related to his new taxon Unwindia, and Witton (2013) assigned it to the family Ornithocheiridae.

facts.statement: A reappraisal by Jiang et al. (2020) recovered Yixianopterus as a basal member of the clade Istiodactyliformes.
facts.quote: A reappraisal of the holotype specimen and phylogenetic analysis by Jiang et al. (2020) recovered Yixianopterus as a basal member of the clade Istiodactyliformes:

facts.statement: It is debated whether Avgodectes, usually considered an embryo, might be a juvenile Yixianopterus, which would give the first name priority.
facts.quote: Una curiosidad es que Avgodectes, que es considerado generalmente como un embrión, quizás sea un ejemplar juvenil de Yixianopterus, en cuyo caso el primer nombre tendría la prioridad.

facts.statement: Yixianopterus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Associated organisms indicate the environment was marine with significant volcanic activity.
facts.quote: Many organisms associated with this layer of the Yixian Formation are aquatic, indicating a marine environment with much volcanic activity.
